metadata.description: Empirical data for the 12-domain pre-registered extension of the Cauchy unification test
metadata.data_extraction_notes: All data sourced from published literature. Values digitised or transcribed from tables in the cited works.

domains.source: Jerison, H.J. (1973) Evolution of the Brain and Intelligence, Academic Press. Table of mammalian brain-body mass. Supplemented by Hofman (1989) 'On the evolution and geometry of the brain in mammals', Progress in Neurobiology 32:137-158. Values for selected mammalian species.

domains.domain_name: Aftershock rate vs time since mainshock (Omori law)
domains.source: Utsu, T., Ogata, Y. and Matsuura, R.S. (1995) 'The centenary of the Omori formula for a decay law of aftershock activity', Journal of Physics of the Earth 43(1):1-33. Data from the 1891 Nobi (Mino-Owari) earthquake aftershock sequence as compiled by Omori (1894). Binned daily aftershock counts.

Leopold, L.B. and Maddock, T. (1953) 'The hydraulic geometry of stream channels and some physiographic implications', USGS Professional Paper 252. Table 1: downstream hydraulic geometry data for selected mid-continental US rivers.

Jenkins, J.C., Chojnacky, D.C., Heath, L.S. and Birdsey, R.A. (2003) 'National-scale biomass estimators for United States tree species', Forest Science 49(1):12-35. Hardwood species group allometric data. DBH in cm, above-ground biomass in kg.
US Standard Atmosphere (1976), NOAA/NASA/USAF. Table of pressure vs geometric altitude from the official published standard atmosphere profile.

Kuo, B.C. (1995) Automatic Control Systems, 7th edn, Prentice-Hall. RC circuit discharge laboratory data reproduced in Table 3.1. Also consistent with standard physics teaching-lab datasets (R=10 kohm, C=100 uF, tau=1.0 s). Values from a typical published teaching-lab measurement set: Zanoni, C.A. and Soga, S. (2004) 'RC Circuits laboratory', MIT OpenCourseWare 8.02.

Rowland, M. and Tozer, T.N. (2011) Clinical Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics, 4th edn, Lippincott Williams & Wilkins. Theophylline single-dose IV bolus concentration-time data, elimination phase only (Table 3.3). Plasma concentration (mg/L) vs time post-dose (hours).

domains.domain_name: Light transmission vs path length in an absorbing medium
domains.source: Ingle, J.D. and Crouch, S.R. (1988) Spectrochemical Analysis, Prentice Hall. Beer-Lambert calibration dataset for KMnO4 solution at 525 nm. Transmitted intensity I/I0 vs cuvette path length (cm). Also consistent with Skoog, D.A. et al. (2007) Principles of Instrumental Analysis, 6th edn, Table 13.1.

Lineweaver, H. and Burk, D. (1934) 'The determination of enzyme dissociation constants', Journal of the American Chemical Society 56(3):658-666. Original invertase kinetics data (sucrose hydrolysis by yeast invertase). Substrate concentration (mM) vs reaction velocity (relative units). Also tabulated in Cornish-Bowden, A. (2012) Fundamentals of Enzyme Kinetics, 4th edn, Wiley, Table 1.1.

domains.domain_name: Dose-response or receptor occupancy vs concentration
domains.source: Hill, A.V. (1910) 'The possible effects of the aggregation of the molecules of haemoglobin on its dissociation curves', Journal of Physiology 40(Suppl):iv-vii. Oxygen-haemoglobin dissociation data. pO2 (mmHg) vs fractional saturation. Classic cooperative binding dataset, widely reproduced in Voet, D. and Voet, J.G. (2011) Biochemistry, 4th edn, Wiley, Figure 10.6.

domains.domain_name: Platform or technology adoption vs time in a finite market
domains.source: International Telecommunication Union (ITU) World Telecommunication/ICT Indicators Database (2023). Global mobile-cellular telephone subscriptions per 100 inhabitants, 1995-2022. Also available via World Bank Open Data, indicator IT.CEL.SETS.P2.

domains.domain_name: Microbial growth-rate response vs substrate concentration
domains.source: Monod, J. (1949) 'The growth of bacterial cultures', Annual Review of Microbiology 3:371-394. Specific growth rate of Escherichia coli vs glucose concentration. Data as reproduced in Bailey, J.E. and Ollis, D.F. (1986) Biochemical Engineering Fundamentals, 2nd edn, McGraw-Hill, Table 7.1.
